what: A cloth (noren curtain) panel hung from its top edge ripples as if swaying in the wind (WebGL · curtains.js plane 60×60). Each Frame follows a random target of 0~2 with very slow damping (.004 at 1440 width), so the intensity rises and falls near the cap (.5 at 1440 width, .08 on phone), the lower it goes the more it folds back and forth, and the edges flare slightly. Folded faces catch the light and only 35% of them are shaded.

options.speed: Ripple time advanced per frame, default 1 (original: .5 when pixel ratio exceeds 1.5)
options.max: Intensity cap — if given, used instead of the per-screen-width table (.08/.1/.2/.3/.5)
options.damping: Rate at which intensity follows the target — used instead of a per-screen-width table (4e-4 … .004)
options.fold: Number of divisions for front and back folds (higher is shallower), default 30
options.[data-fx-part=cloth]: One fabric panel (child) — the inner Uses it as is, or if absent, paints with the background color and label of the inner .wf-img (or itself). Hidden once the panel is ready

note: The original contains a mouse-position formula but never passes the mouse, so it is always (0, 0) — the part reduced the formula using that value (yAttenuation .5). The canvas is laid over the element and does not follow scroll (it moves together with the element). With reduced motion it does not draw and leaves the cloth image as is
